subsystems.name: Positioning and isolation
subsystems.role: holds each tip within fractions of a nanometre of the target.

subsystems.name: Control and feedback
subsystems.role: reads the tunnelling current and adjusts tip height and position in real time.

subsystems.name: Atom source and delivery
subsystems.role: supplies the atoms to be placed.

subsystems.name: Substrate and environment
subsystems.role: provides a clean, cold surface on which to build.
parts: atomically flat substrate (e.g. copper or silicon)

subsystems.name: Verification and metrology
subsystems.role: confirms that each atom sits where intended.

subsystems.name: Parallel operation and automation
subsystems.role: coordinates many tips to build simultaneously and correct errors.

buildSteps.title: Design the structure atom by atom
buildSteps.detail: Computational chemistry specifies every atom, bond and layer before any physical work begins.

buildSteps.title: Prepare the environment
buildSteps.detail: An ultra-high-vacuum chamber is pumped down and cooled to a few kelvin so atoms stay put and contamination is negligible.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the probe array
buildSteps.detail: Metal or carbon tips are etched or grown to atomic sharpness, then integrated with piezoelectric actuators on a chip.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate tip positions
buildSteps.detail: Each tip's location and response are mapped, and control sequences are written to move atoms reliably.

buildSteps.title: Place atoms
buildSteps.detail: A tip picks up a single atom, moves it to the target site, and deposits it; the structure is built layer by layer.

buildSteps.title: Verify and correct
buildSteps.detail: The surface is imaged after each step, and misplaced atoms are removed or repositioned.

buildSteps.title: Scale up parallelism
buildSteps.detail: Many tips operate at once, with automated feedback to keep them aligned and to fix errors faster than humans can.

buildSteps.title: Package and interconnect
buildSteps.detail: For a working device, the atomically precise part is connected to macroscopic electrical or mechanical interfaces without disturbing it.

prerequisites.why: the only demonstrated way to image and touch individual atoms on a surface.
single atoms and molecules have been moved, but only at extremely slow speeds over tiny areas.
MEMS cantilever arrays exist for data storage, but none yet combine thousands of tips for atom placement.
without them, atoms diffuse, oxidise or are buried by contamination.
small molecules can be modelled accurately, but predicting macroscopic assemblies remains hard.
building a macroscopic object atom by atom would require detecting and fixing mistakes at a rate far beyond current capability.

pathway.milestone: single-tip atomic manipulation in research labs, such as writing with xenon atoms at IBM in 1989
pathway.unlocks: proof that atoms can be positioned one by one.

pathway.milestone: small parallel arrays of ten to a hundred tips patterning nanoscale features
pathway.unlocks: faster fabrication of simple atomically precise structures over micrometre areas.

pathway.milestone: automated assembly of nanoscale components such as molecular motors or logic elements
pathway.unlocks: test beds for error correction and design tools.

pathway.milestone: massively parallel arrays with real-time verification building micron-scale objects
pathway.unlocks: practical atomically precise manufacturing for specialised devices.

pathway.milestone: macroscopic objects built atom by atom at useful speed
pathway.unlocks: a general bottom-up manufacturing technology, if the extreme parallelism and speed barriers can be overcome.
